text:
maya: Heads-up — we should align on label taxonomy for the gateway + routing dashboards before the next quarter. I keep seeing different `route`/`path` labels and it's making joins painful.
sam: Yup. Noticed `route` vs `endpoint` in a few dashboards. Also some metrics have `model` and some `model_variant`.
devon: Cardinality is my worry — route + user_id + model_variant can explode. We need clear guidance on which labels are allowed on high-cardinality metrics.
liam: Agreed. Proposal: keep these labels for high-cardinality metrics: `route`, `region`, `customer_tier`. For lower-cardinality debug metrics we can include `model_variant` and `requestor`.
tori: Also want a standardized naming prefix for gateway metrics: `gateway_` or `redwood_gateway_`? Helps with dashboards and ingestion rules.
maya: Let's standardize on `gateway_` prefix for public ingestion so it stays short in Prom. Internal infra metrics can use `infra_`.
sam: Can we have an allowlist/denylist per metric class? e.g., histograms and counters get only these labels, debug_gauges can have more.
devon: Yes. Define classes: `hot` (high-cardinality, high-throughput), `warm` (moderate), `cold` (low throughput, debug). Map allowed labels per class.
liam: For rollout UX we should also add `canary` boolean label on request traces so console can surface cohort performance. That one is low-cardinality.
tori: Example metric proto for `hot` request latency:
```
# gateway request latency (hot)
gateway_request_latency_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/generate",region="us-west1",customer_tier="pro",le="0.1"} 42
```
sam: That looks good. For `model_variant` let's capture it only on `warm`/`cold` classes to avoid cardinality blowup.
maya: Ops question — any downstream dashboards that rely on current inconsistent labels? We need a migration plan and aliasing.
liam: A few SLO dashboards use `endpoint` right now. We can add relabel/alias rules in Prom remote_write config for 2 weeks, then migrate dashboards.
devon: We should also publish a small code snippet for relabeling in prometheus `relabel_configs` so teams can test locally.
tori: I'll draft a doc with the taxonomy + allowed labels matrix and the relabel snippets.
maya: Action items: tori to draft doc by EOD Fri, liam to add relabel rules in staging, sam to run cardinality simulation on prod sample, devon to list dashboards that need update.
liam: I'll create a staging PR for the relabels and ping #eng-platform when it's ready.
sam: For the simulation, what's the dataset? Can you point me to a query or export?
devon: Use the 24h gateway scrape sample in `s3://redwood-telemetry/samples/gateway-24h.parquet` and run the cardinality checker script in `infra/tools/cardinality-check`.
maya: Cool — please add owners in the doc. If we can get this done before the next release, rollout dashboards will be much cleaner.
infra-bot: Deploy pipeline: relabel-pr -> staging tests -> canary -> prod. Will post status.
tori: Draft is up: https://internal.redwood.ai/docs/label-taxonomy (WIP). Feedback welcome.
maya: :thumbsup: Fine-grained but actionable. Let's reconvene after PRs land.
liam: FYI — one small caveat: some legacy exporters embed the route in `handler` label. We should include that in the migration notes.
devon: Noted. Also recommend adding `policy` label for routing policy (e.g., `quota`, `fallback`, `direct`) on routing decision metrics — low-cardinality and useful for dashboards.
sam: OK to add `policy` on `warm` metrics.
maya: Great. Meeting adjourned. Thanks everyone.
